reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 13.1 is the operative grant for the hosted Services and expressly limits it to 'Customer alone', excludes Affiliates and contractors, and makes it revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — walk-away territory under the rule, and the fallback (Affiliates covered, even on notice) is not met for the Services because 13.2 is confined to paid-up/embedded software and Vendor Technology and 13.3 addresses only transfer and revocation, not Affiliate use.

The redline reaches the playbook position with the operative changes required by the redline guidance: it extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, deletes discretionary revocation, and adds Affiliate/successor transferability by cross-reference to Section 13.3, which also resolves the direct contradiction with 13.2/13.3 rather than creating new terms.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.79 changed-character ratio) is not disqualifying here: every material term of the original 13.1 (Customer-only, non-transferable, revocable at will) was adverse, so a whole-clause rewrite is the smallest edit that reaches the position, and nothing beneficial to Customer was removed.

The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (Affiliate coverage on written notice; successor transfer in an M&A transaction) without over-reaching or lecturing.
No double-flagging: the finding is confined to the licence grant scope and does not re-litigate the assignment or IP ownership terms.
